Third person action MOBA with mythological gods as the thematic.
Can be competitive or casual depending on the mode, and most entertained I've been in a MOBA in general.

The game is very fun to play, especially if you are into mythology and always wanted to do battle alongside a Norse God.

There is a meta...and where there is a meta there are balance issues. And yes, there is a fair deal of powercreep that does not exist in Dota 2; that is my main issue with the game.

Its not P2W, but then again I am not sure how a MOBA could be p2W. Be aware that not all the gods are unlocked at first; you are given some for free, but then have to use in-game currency to buy more. Before investing money in a god, you can try them all out in training mode for free, and you can rent the gods for a period of time.There are some promotionals to unlock some of the gods for free, but it will still take some time to unlock all the ones you want.

The community is not as cancerous as others in that players are willing to help others. It can be cancerous with regards to the amount of skill some players have, and their inability to fulfill their role in a team.

As someone who bought the ability to have the full roster early on in the games life, I enjoy this game. I have a particular fondness for mythology and folklore, so it's always enjoyable to go through the roster and see how they've chosen to depict each individual character. I have to admit that the decision to include skins for characters who are from pop culture goes a bit against the base concept of being mythology/folklore but I figure it likely was a way for them to make some extra cash and grab a few more peoples attention so I really cant fault them for it.

I can, however, see why people would find this game to be frustrating if they do not have access to the full roster of characters. Even with the rotating 'free' characters, you do not get access to enough to keep the game engaging. There is an abundance of microtransactions, moreso if you include skins, and I don't believe the game offers the 'full unlock' any longer because it means they'd be losing out on money.

Unfortunately with the release of Smite 2, I'm not sure if this game is going to be seeing any further updates.

Smite and I have a love/hate relationship. I spend all my time with it but it still ♥♥♥♥s me over. Like all MOBAs, Smite has a toxic community. To be frank, I wouldn't recommend new players to try this out alone since matchmaking isn't always fair and it's way more fun with friends anyway especially with the voice chat that they've added. I love god and goddess folklore so playing characters with abilities that match their lore and the variety and ever expanding pantheons is what makes Smite stand out.

If you're coming from another MOBA, I feel like building and items are even more important here so if you're new, read guides! The builds online have been super helpful.

All in all, I do recommend Smite. Among all the salty spammers, DCers, and the "VER VVX"s, there are small factions of the community that are friendly and are willing to help.
